findings.source_passage: The very phrases were worn so threadbare that they evoked no image except that of a turbaned 'character' leaking sawdust at every pore as he pursued a tiger through the Bois de Boulogne.
findings.source_locator: After Gatsby describes living 'like a young rajah' collecting rubies and hunting big game
findings.why_it_matters: This is one of the most distinctively voiced satirical sentences in the chapter—Nick's incredulous deflation of Gatsby's fabrications. Its total absence erases a key beat of Nick's ironic consciousness and the novel's critique of Gatsby's self-invention.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the sentence verbatim immediately after the rajah passage; it is short and can replace no more than one draft sentence.

findings.source_passage: Little Montenegro! He lifted up the words and nodded at them—with his smile. The smile comprehended Montenegro's troubled history and sympathized with the brave struggles of the Montenegrin people.
findings.source_locator: After Gatsby says 'even Montenegro, little Montenegro down on the Adriatic Sea!'
findings.why_it_matters: This is a critically canonical passage: the 'smile' passage is one of the primary loci in the critical tradition for Gatsby's performed charisma and Nick's fascination. It also sets up the recurring motif of Gatsby's smile. Its erasure is a major interpretive loss.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the Montenegro smile elaboration verbatim after the exclamation; it runs only four sentences and is irreplaceable.

findings.source_passage: Then it was all true. I saw the skins of tigers flaming in his palace on the Grand Canal; I saw him opening a chest of rubies to ease, with their crimson-lighted depths, the gnawings of his broken heart.
findings.source_locator: After Gatsby shows Nick the Oxford photograph and the medal
findings.why_it_matters: This is one of the most-quoted passages in the novel and a critical touchstone for Nick's romantic complicity in Gatsby's myth. Its absence removes the moment when Nick's skepticism collapses into belief, which is interpretively essential.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert verbatim after the description of the Oxford photograph; three sentences that can stand alone.

findings.source_passage: It never occurred to me that one man could start to play with the faith of fifty million people—with the single-mindedness of a burglar blowing a safe.
findings.source_locator: After Gatsby reveals Wolfshiem fixed the World's Series
findings.why_it_matters: This is a famous, widely-quoted sentence and the passage the critical tradition returns to when discussing the corruption beneath Gatsby's world. The draft preserves the bare fact but erases the signature phrasing entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full paragraph beginning 'The idea staggered me…' including the 'burglar blowing a safe' sentence verbatim.

findings.source_passage: that resourcefulness of movement that is so peculiarly American—that comes, I suppose, with the absence of lifting work in youth and, even more, with the formless grace of our nervous, sporadic games.
findings.source_locator: Description of Gatsby balancing on the car dashboard
findings.why_it_matters: This is interpretively weighted voice prose—Nick's essayistic theorizing about American class and physical ease—compressed to the bare label 'that American resourcefulness of movement,' erasing the digressive analytical voice that defines Nick's narration.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full parenthetical clause beginning 'that comes, I suppose, with the absence of lifting work in youth' to preserve the narrator's voice register.

findings.source_passage: A dead man passed us in a hearse heaped with blooms, followed by two carriages with drawn blinds… As we crossed Blackwell's Island a limousine passed us, driven by a white chauffeur, in which sat three modish negroes, two bucks and a girl.
findings.source_locator: Immediately after 'the city seen for the first time' passage, crossing the Queensboro Bridge
findings.why_it_matters: This passage—the hearse, the mourners, the Black passengers—is part of the Queensboro Bridge threshold sequence and carries significant critical weight regarding race, death, and democratic possibility; it gives the 'anything can happen' thought its full context.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the hearse and limousine passage between the 'mystery and beauty' sentence and the 'Anything can happen' thought; it is five sentences and essential to the bridge sequence.

findings.source_passage: this clean, hard, limited person, who dealt in universal scepticism, and who leaned back jauntily just within the circle of my arm.
findings.source_locator: Nick's turn toward Jordan after learning of Gatsby's plan, in the victoria
findings.why_it_matters: 'Who dealt in universal scepticism' is the defining characterization of Jordan Baker at this moment; its removal reduces a precise character insight to mere physical description and weakens the contrast with Gatsby's romanticism.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'who dealt in universal scepticism' in the Jordan description; it is six words and fits naturally.

findings.source_passage: Reach me a rose, honey, and pour me a last drop into that there crystal glass.
findings.source_locator: Young ladies' speech at the opening of the chapter
findings.why_it_matters: The closing line of the young ladies' direct speech is rhythmically distinct and captures the studied, campy idiom of Gatsby's female guests; its omission slightly flattens the satirical register of the opening.
findings.suggested_fix: Append the line as the close of the young ladies' quoted speech.

summary: The draft erases four high-severity signature passages—the 'leaking sawdust' satirical aside, the Montenegro smile elaboration, the 'tigers flaming in his palace' moment of Nick's surrender, and the 'faith of fifty million people / burglar blowing a safe' World Series sentence—plus the hearse-and-limousine bridge sequence and two notable voice-flattening compressions, collectively gutting the chapter's most critically engaged and rhetorically distinctive prose.
